validation.code: Use up to {max} letters, digits or - _ . /, starting with a letter or digit.
validation.email: Enter an email address like name@example.com.
validation.phone: Use digits, spaces or dashes, optionally starting with +.
validation.date: Enter a full date: day, month and year.

validation.confirmationBeforeJoining: The confirmation date can't be before the joining date.
validation.passwordMismatch: The passwords don't match. Type the new password again.
validation.passwordSame: Choose a password that is different from your current one.
validation.shiftEndsAtStart: A shift can't end at the time it starts. For a night shift, enter an end time earlier in the day, e.g. 22:00 to 06:00.
validation.breakTooLong: The break must be shorter than the shift.
validation.fullDayTooLong: A full day can't need more than the shift has after its break: {hours}.
validation.halfDayTooLong: The half-day threshold can't be more than a full day.
validation.punchWindowTooLong: Before + the shift + after can't add up to more than 24 hours, or one punch could count for two days. Shorten the window.
validation.patternEmpty: Choose at least one day off.
validation.patternDuplicate: A day is listed more than once.
validation.patternEveryWeekAndSome: A day that is off every week can't also be off in particular weeks.
validation.patternEveryDay: Leave at least one working day in the week.
validation.rangeOrder: The end date can't be before the start date.
validation.rangeTooLong: Choose at most {max} days, both dates included.

hints.code: Short, shown in roster cells. Stored in capitals, e.g. GEN or NIGHT-A.
hints.graceIn: Minutes after the start before arriving counts as late. 0 to {max}.
hints.graceOut: Minutes before the end that leaving doesn't count as early. 0 to {max}.
hints.fullDay: Worked time that makes a full day.
hints.halfDay: Worked time below this, but above none, is a half day.
hints.windowBefore: How early a punch still counts for this shift.
hints.windowAfter: How late a punch still counts for this shift.

explain.enterTimes: Enter a start and an end time.
explain.sameTimes: A shift can't start and end at the same time.
explain.night: Runs overnight, from <start></start> to <end></end> (+1 is the next day), {length} in all. The whole shift belongs to the day it starts: a Monday 22:00 start is Monday's attendance, punches after midnight included (BR-12).
explain.break: {minutes} minutes are deducted from the time between first in and last out (BR-02), leaving {paid} of work in a full shift. The break isn't tied to a time of day, so the timeline draws it in the middle.
explain.noBreak: No break: worked time is the whole time between first in and last out (BR-02).
explain.graceIn: Arriving up to <until></until> isn't late; arriving after it is (BR-03). With {minutes} minutes of grace, someone 6 minutes behind <start></start> is on time.
explain.noGraceIn: No grace: arriving even a minute after <start></start> is late.
explain.graceOut: Leaving from <from></from> isn't an early out; leaving before it is. That is {minutes} minutes before <end></end>.
explain.noGraceOut: No grace: leaving even a minute before <end></end> is an early out.
explain.graceIsNotTime: Grace doesn't add working time or move the shift. It only decides where late-in and early-out begin.
explain.halfDay: Worked time below {hours}, but above none, makes the day a half day (BR-04).
explain.fullDay: {hours} of worked time makes a full day.
explain.absent: A working day with no punch at all, that isn't a weekly off, holiday or approved leave, is absent (BR-01).
explain.window: A punch from <from></from> to <until></until> counts for this shift's day. A punch outside it is looked for on another day, which is what keeps both punches of a night shift on its start date.
explain.windowIsNotGrace: The punch window isn't grace: it decides which day a punch belongs to, never whether it is late.

hints.name: Say what it is, e.g. “Friday + alternate Saturdays”.

patterns.weekOfMonthNote: Week 2 means the second of that weekday in the month (days 8–14), not the second row of a calendar. So alternate Saturdays are the 2nd and 4th; a 5th one only happens in some months.
